text: Richard Stallman is a computer scientist and software freedom advocate born in 1953 in New York City. He developed a strong interest in computers during his youth and pursued a degree in physics at Harvard University before joining the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. In 1983, he founded the GNU Project, a free and open-source operating system, and established the Free Software Foundation to promote software freedom and protect users' rights to modify and redistribute software. Stallman is known for popularizing the concept of copyleft, a legal mechanism that ensures software remains free. He has been a vocal critic of proprietary software and software patents, advocating for software freedom as a moral and ethical imperative. Stallman promotes the use of the term "free software" to emphasize freedom, not just cost, and has consistently opposed the use of terms like "open source" that he believes obscure the philosophical underpinnings of software freedom. He has also been a prominent figure in promoting digital privacy, resisting surveillance, and supporting the development of free software alternatives. Stallman is known for his strong advocacy for user freedom, his principled stance on software ethics, and his influence on the open-source movement. He has received numerous awards, including the MacArthur "Genius" Fellowship and the National Medal of Science, and has been recognized for his contributions to computing and free software. His work has had a lasting impact on the development of free and open-source software, shaping modern computing practices and advocating for a more ethical and user-centered approach to technology.
